sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and random input ranges
sections.what: Imports the pipeline steps and sets the random input rules: start days from 0 to 1,500, durations from 0 to 730 days, and short suffix names of up to 8 letters or digits. It also limits the test to 12 examples and turns off the time limit.
sections.why: Keeps random inputs realistic and the run count small enough to finish in a normal test session.
sections.watch_out: Raising the example count or the time limit makes the test much slower.

sections.name: test_generated_schedules_preserve_projects_and_model_invariants
sections.title: Random schedule invariant checks
sections.what: Writes a random three-activity CSV across two projects, ingests it, and then checks that the project IDs and activity counts are right, that every project model has unique component IDs and finite positions, that no activity has a finish before its start, and that every activity ends up as physical, abstract or unrepresented.
sections.why: Likely reason: these checks cover the rules a schedule must follow after every step, so random data can reveal breaks that fixed examples would not.
sections.watch_out: The check that every activity is accounted for depends on the sets physical, abstract and unrepresented staying in sync with the model.

summary: Generates many random schedules and checks that the ingestion, model and render steps keep projects separate, produce finite positions, and account for every activity.
purpose: Finds edge cases that hand-written examples would miss, using random start dates, durations and names.
why: Likely reason: the schedule pipeline has many possible inputs, so random testing checks rules that must hold for all of them.
how: A hypothesis decorator supplies up to 12 random sets of start offset, duration and suffix. Each set writes a small three-activity CSV with two projects, ingests it into a database, builds a model and render manifest for each project, and checks several invariants.
inputs: Random integers and short text generated by the hypothesis library, plus a temporary folder from pytest.
outputs: Pass or fail results. Temporary CSV and database files are written to the temporary folder.
risks: Each generated case writes a database, so the run is slower than a normal unit test. The deadline is turned off, so a very slow case will not fail on time alone.
debug: When hypothesis finds a failing case, it prints the exact input values. Use them to rebuild the CSV by hand and run the ingest and model steps one at a time.
